nodes.summary: A group $G$ acts faithfully on a regular rooted tree by finite-state automorphisms when there are a natural number $d \ge 2$ and an injective group homomorphism $\varphi$ from $G$ to the group of permutations of the set of finite words over $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$ such that $\varphi(g)$ is a finite-state automorphism of the $d$-regular rooted tree for every $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Faithful actions by finite-state tree automorphisms

nodes.summary: For every integer $d \ge 2$, the group of finite-state automorphisms of the $d$-regular rooted tree has an irreducible system of generators: a set $S$ of elements of the group that generates the group and no proper subset of which generates the group.
nodes.title: Lavrenyuk's theorem on irreducible generators of finite-state automorphism groups

nodes.summary: Kourovka Problem 16.86 (Sushchanskiĭ): irreducible generators of finite-state automorphism groups. The statement that for every integer $d \ge 2$ the group of finite-state automorphisms of the $d$-regular rooted tree has an irreducible system of generators: a set $S$ of elements of the group that generates the group and no proper subset of which generates the group.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.86 (Sushchanskiĭ): irreducible generators of finite-state automorphism groups

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, consider the $d$-regular rooted tree whose vertices are the finite words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$. The group of finite-state automorphisms of this tree is the subgroup of the group of all permutations of the words generated by the tree automorphisms that have only finitely many distinct sections.
nodes.title: Finite-state automorphisms of a regular rooted tree

nodes.summary: The answer to Kourovka Problem 16.34 is negative: there exist $d, k \in \mathbb{N}$ and finite-state automorphisms $g_0, \dots, g_{k-1}$ of the $d$-regular rooted tree such that no algorithm decides, given two words in the $g_i$ and their inverses, whether the elements they spell are conjugate in the group generated by $g_0, \dots, g_{k-1}$.
nodes.title: Finite-state tree automorphism groups with undecidable conjugacy problem

nodes.summary: The proposition that every finitely generated group of finite-state automorphisms of a regular rooted tree has decidable conjugacy problem: for all $d, k \in \mathbb{N}$ and all finite-state automorphisms $g_0, \dots, g_{k-1}$ of the $d$-regular rooted tree, some algorithm decides, given two words in the $g_i$ and their inverses, whether the elements they spell are conjugate in the group generated by…
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.34: conjugacy in finite-state automorphism groups

nodes.summary: For all groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ and $H$ each act faithfully on a regular rooted tree by finite-state automorphisms, then their free product $G \ast H$ acts faithfully on some regular rooted tree by finite-state automorphisms.
nodes.title: Fedorova–Oliynyk theorem (Kourovka Problem 16.85)

nodes.summary: The statement that for all groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ and $H$ each act faithfully on a regular rooted tree by finite-state automorphisms (the two trees may have different degrees), then so does their free product $G \ast H$.
nodes.title: Finite-state actions of free products (Kourovka Problem 16.85)

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, let $X^*$ be the set of finite words over $X = \{0, \dots, d-1\}$. A permutation $f$ of $X^*$ is a finite-state automorphism when it is an automorphism of the $d$-regular rooted tree and its sections at the vertices $u \in X^*$ form a finite set of maps $X^* \to X^*$.
nodes.title: Finite-state automorphisms of the regular rooted tree (Kourovka 16.85)

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a permutation $f$ of the finite words over $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$ is a finite-state automorphism of the $d$-regular rooted tree when it is an automorphism of the tree and the sections of $f$ at all vertices $u$ form a finite set of maps.
nodes.title: Finite-state automorphism of the regular rooted tree

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number and let $X^*$ be the set of finite words over the alphabet $X = \{0, \dots, d-1\}$, the vertices of the $d$-regular rooted tree. A permutation $f$ of $X^*$ is a tree automorphism when, for all words $u$ and $v$, the word $f(u)$ has the same length $|u|$ as $u$ and the first $|u|$ letters of $f(uv)$ form the word $f(u)$, where $uv$ denotes concatenation.
nodes.title: Automorphisms of the regular rooted tree (Kourovka 16.85)

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the vertices of the $d$-regular rooted tree are the finite words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$. A permutation $f$ of this set of words is a tree automorphism when, for all words $u$ and $v$, writing $|u|$ for the length of $u$ and $uv$ for the concatenation of $u$ and $v$, the word $f(u)$ has length $|u|$ and the first $|u|$ letters of $f(uv)$ form $f(u)$.
nodes.title: Automorphism of the regular rooted tree

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, the $d$-regular rooted tree has as vertices the finite words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$; write $vw$ for the concatenation of words $v$ and $w$. The root is the empty word and the children of a word $v$ are the words $vi$ for letters $i$. A permutation $g$ of the words is a tree automorphism when for all words $v$ and $w$ there is a word $u$ of the same length as $w$ with…
nodes.title: Automorphisms of the regular rooted tree

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, let $X^*$ be the set of finite words over $X = \{0, \dots, d-1\}$, let $f$ be a permutation of $X^*$ and let $u \in X^*$, of length $|u|$. The section (state) of $f$ at $u$ is the map $X^* \to X^*$ sending a word $w$ to the word obtained from $f(uw)$ by deleting its first $|u|$ letters (all of them if it has fewer), where $uw$ denotes concatenation.
nodes.title: Section of a permutation of the tree at a vertex (Kourovka 16.85)

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, let $g$ be a permutation of the finite words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$ and let $v$ be a word. The section (state) of $g$ at $v$ is the map sending a word $w$ to the word obtained from $g(vw)$ by deleting its first $|g(v)|$ letters, where $vw$ is the concatenation of $v$ and $w$ and $|g(v)|$ is the length of $g(v)$. When $g$ is a tree automorphism, the image of $w$ is the word…
nodes.title: Section of a word permutation at a vertex

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $f$ be a permutation of the finite words over $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$ (the vertices of the $d$-regular rooted tree) and let $u$ be a word, of length $|u|$. The section (state) of $f$ at $u$ is the map sending each word $w$ to the word obtained from $f(uw)$ by deleting its first $|u|$ letters, where $uw$ is the concatenation of $u$ and $w$.
nodes.title: Section of a map of the regular rooted tree at a vertex

nodes.summary: For $d, k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $g_0, \dots, g_{k-1}$ be permutations of the finite words over $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$, and let $w$ be a word whose letters are pairs $(i, b)$ with $i < k$ and $b$ a boolean. The value of $w$ is the element of the group generated by $g_0, \dots, g_{k-1}$ obtained by multiplying, from left to right, $g_i$ for each letter $(i, \mathrm{true})$ and $g_i^{-1}$ for each letter…
nodes.title: Value of a word in the generators

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
